sentences.text: Though the matter is listed for orders with the consent of the parties, matter is taken up for final disposal.

2. Heard learned counsel Sri.Karthik Ganachari for Sri.S.S.Gundi, Sri.Anand Kumar and Sri.Chandrashekar Hosmani.
3. Insurance company is in appeal challenging both quantum of compensation as well as on liability of the insurance company to pay the compensation in respect of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.734/2015 dated 31.12.2016 on the file of Addl. MACT, Saundatti, Belagavi district.
4. Fact which is not in dispute in this appeal is loss of life of Somappa Maramannavar in a road traffic accident that occurred on 30.08.2014 at about 4.30 p.m., involving Tata Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-11/A-0799.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:928 5.
Admittedly, deceased was aged 65 years as per the claim petition.
The tribunal granted compensation in a sum of Rs.12,35,056/- and same is not challenged by claimants.

6. Reiterating the grounds urged in the appeal learned counsel Sri.Karthik Ganachari contended that the driver of the vehicle did not possess proper endorsement to drive the Tata Magic vehicle and therefore, sought for allowing the appeal.

7. Insofar as quantum of compensation is concerned, tribunal has taken into consideration Rs.20,000/- as income in the absence of proper proof of income of a deceased person aged 65 years and therefore, tribunal has erred in awarding compensation in a sum of Rs.12,35,056/- and sought for reassessment of compensation.
8. Per contra, learned counsel Sri.K.Anand Kumar and Sri.C.M.Hosamani for counsel for respondent No.5 supported the impugned judgment.
Learned counsel Sri. Anand kumar contends that the deceased was doing milk vending and agriculture and therefore, tribunal assessing the income at Rs.20,000/- p.m is just and proper.
The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Kashavva W/O. Somappa ... on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115115405/

sentences.text: 3 10. Sri
.C.M.Hosamani, counsel contended that since the vehicle was duly insured, insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.
11. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this court has perused the material available on record meticulously.

12. On such perusal of the material on record, it is not in dispute that somappa Maramannavar having lost his life in the road traffic accident that occurred on 30.08.2014 at 4.30 pm involving Tata Magic vehicle bearing No.KA-11/A- 0799.
13.

Admittedly, the driver of the vehicle did possess the license for driving the light motor vehicle but there is no NC: 2024:KHC-D:928 proper endorsement for riding the vehicle which was involved in transferring the passengers.
14. Applying the principles of law enunciated in the case of Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668, the insurance company cannot avoid the liability.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the first ground on which appeal is sought to be allowed cannot be countenanced in law.

15. Coming to the question of quantum of compensation, there is sufficient force in the argument put forth on behalf of the appellant that the tribunal has wrongly taken monthly income in a sum of Rs.20,000/- p.m. while assessing the quantum of compensation in the absence of proper proof of income.

16. For an accidental death of the year 2014, usually this court assess the monthly income in a sum of Rs.7,500/- p.m., 1/3 income is to be deducted from the said income for the purpose of personal expenses.

Taking into consideration of the same, the loss of future income is to be reassessed as under:
Rs.7500X12X2/3X7=Rs.4,20,000/-.
Tribunal has wrongly assessed the compensation on the other heads as well.

18. Following the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, and in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076, the claimants are entitled to Rs.1,60,000/- towards loss of filial affection, on the conventional head claimants are entitled for R.30,000/-.
19.

In view of the foregoing discussions, the following :
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) As against sum of Rs.12,35,056/-, claimants are entitled for sum of Rs.6,10,000-00 payable by the appellant to the claimants with interest at 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization of entire amount.
iii) Apportionment and other aspects are proportionately to be made in accordance with the order of the trial court.
iv) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the tribunal for disbursement in accordance with law.
